# Gelabber v0.9.0

Integrated through #430, #435, #433 and #459 into `v0.9` and the version PR
into `main`.

**After the update, sign in once.** The desktop app is new: your server
address and most settings come along, the sign-in does not. On Windows,
pin Gelabber to the taskbar again if you had pinned it.

The desktop app is now a native app. It replaces the Tauri app of 0.5 to
0.8.10. The server, the web interface and the Compose setup are the same as
in v0.8.10, apart from their version and dependency updates. There is no
database migration, and `.env`, `compose.yaml` and `Caddyfile` change only
in their image pins.

## Desktop: the native app (#430, #433)

- **One Rust process without a web view.** The window is drawn with egui on
  the GPU (wgpu). Chat, direct messages, settings, server settings, voice,
  video and Go Live run in the app itself; calls use the native media core
  (mediasoup through libwebrtc) the Tauri app already used.
- **Around the window:** a tray icon with unread dots, desktop
  notifications (D-Bus on Linux, toasts on Windows), one instance per user,
  and global push-to-talk (the GlobalShortcuts portal on Linux, a keyboard
  hook on Windows).
- **Sign-in** is kept in the system keyring (Secret Service on Linux,
  Credential Manager on Windows), or else in `session.json`, readable by the
  user only.
- **Windows x64:** the app updates itself, as the Tauri app did. It checks
  shortly after the start and then every 6 hours, checks the installer's
  signature with the same key, and does not install during a call or in
  the minute after it. The WebView2 runtime is no longer needed.
- **Linux x64:** no in-app updater. The app says when a new version is out
  and points to pacman or the release page. It needs Vulkan
  (`vulkan-icd-loader` and the GPU's Vulkan driver) and no longer needs
  WebKitGTK, libsoup or GTK.
- The settings page shows the push-to-talk bind for Hyprland with the new
  app id (see below).

## Updating the desktop app

- **Windows:** installed Tauri apps from 0.7.0 on offer the update as
  usual. It installs the native app into the same folder
  (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Gelabber`), closes and removes `gelabber-desktop.exe`,
  points the Start menu and Desktop shortcuts to `gelabber.exe` and starts
  it. Then sign in once. Apps of 0.5 and 0.6 have no updater: install by
  hand.
- **Windows, by hand:** `gelabber-native-windows-x64-setup.exe`. It is not
  Authenticode-signed, so SmartScreen warns ("Der Computer wurde durch
  Windows geschützt"): click "Weitere Informationen", then "Trotzdem
  ausführen". Download it only from the release page.
- **Arch / Omarchy:** `pacman -Syu` (or `yay -Syu`). The package keeps its
  name, `gelabber-desktop`, and replaces the Tauri app: files move from
  `/opt/gelabber-desktop` to `/opt/gelabber`, the command is `gelabber`
  (`gelabber-desktop` stays as a link for keybinds and autostarts). It also
  replaces the beta package `gelabber-desktop-native`. WebKitGTK, libsoup
  and GTK stay installed as orphans if nothing else needs them
  (`pacman -Qdt` lists them).
- **Linux tarball:** download `gelabber-native-linux-x64.tar.gz` and start
  `./gelabber` (before: `./gelabber-desktop`). Keep
  `libgelabber_media.so` next to it.
- **New asset names:** `gelabber-native-windows-x64-setup.exe` (with
  `.sha256` and `.sig`), `gelabber-native-linux-x64.tar.gz`,
  `latest-native.json` and `latest.json`. Links to
  `releases/latest/download/gelabber-desktop-*` stop working.
- **Hyprland push-to-talk:** the app registers as `gelabber`, not
  `gelabber-desktop`. Change the bind in `hyprland.conf` to
  `bind = , F13, global, gelabber:push-to-talk` (your key instead of F13).
  KDE and GNOME may ask for the key again.
- The desktop entry is now `gelabber.desktop` (window class `gelabber`).
  Launcher or dock pins and window rules for `gelabber-desktop` may need
  to be set again.

## What comes over, and what starts fresh

On its first start, and only then, the app takes over what the Tauri app
kept:

- From `legacy-settings.json`, which the Tauri app of 0.8.10 writes. Start
  0.8.10 once before updating to get the newest copy.
- Otherwise, for 0.8.9 and older, the same entries from the Tauri app's
  WebView storage (WebView2 on Windows, WebKitGTK on Linux).

Taken over: voice and device settings (including desktop notifications and
the message sound), the Live sound choice, interface preferences (UI scale,
compact rooms, reduced motion), per-user volumes, and unsent drafts younger
than 7 days. The server address stays, because the config folder is shared.
Nothing is overwritten, and the old files stay on disk.

Starts fresh:

- **The sign-in:** sign in once.
- The last server, channel and direct message you had open.
- Whether the member panel was hidden.
- The local theme choice. Your themes come back with the account.

## Known limits of the native app

These worked in the Tauri app and do not yet in 0.9. The browser has them
all; there is no Tauri app to fall back to.

- **Wayland:** closing the window ends the app, and a running call with it;
  close-to-tray works only on X11 and Windows. The tray icon and "Beenden"
  stay. A click on a notification may not bring the window to the front.
- No spell check in the message box, and no password manager or autofill
  on the sign-in screen.
- Message text cannot be selected with the mouse; use "Text kopieren" in
  the message menu.
- No right-to-left text.
- Screen readers: new messages are not announced, and the UI language is
  not set for them.
- Video and audio attachments are downloads, without a player. YouTube
  previews open in the browser.
- The microphone test only shows the level; it records nothing to play
  back.
- In the message list, only Page Up and Page Down move by keyboard.

Migration limits:

- On Windows, settings in WebView2's newer SQLite storage (an Edge
  experiment) are not read; they are logged and lost. This affects only
  updates from 0.8.9 and older.
- The installer ends the Tauri app with `taskkill /F`. Changes made shortly
  before the update may not have reached the disk.
- A taskbar pin to the old `gelabber-desktop.exe` likely stops working: pin
  Gelabber again.

## Server and web

- No product change: the API, the media server and the web client are the
  same as in v0.8.10. Dependency updates: tokio 1.54.1 and uuid 1.29.0
  (#451, #452), the web client's dependencies (#445–#449), the node and
  nginx base images and the Go builder of the MinIO images (#442), and the
  GitHub actions (#444).
- The native app does not check the server's version. It speaks the API of
  0.8.9 and 0.8.10, which 0.9.0 keeps; servers older than 0.8.9 were not
  tried. Update the server first or together with the apps.
- The web client keeps its code for the Tauri app for 0.9, because
  installed Tauri apps load it until they have updated.

## Upgrade notes

- The image pins `GELABBER_{API,WEB,MEDIA}_IMAGE` move together to
  `v0.9.0`. The order does not matter for this release.
- **Rollback, server:** go back to the v0.8.10 image set, all three
  together. The database is unchanged.
- **Rollback, desktop:** there is no automatic way back.
  - Windows: install v0.8.10's `gelabber-desktop-windows-x64-setup.exe` by
    hand (not tested over the native app), and switch off its update check,
    because its updater would offer 0.9 again.
  - Arch: `pacman -U` the 0.8.10 package from the pacman cache; the
    repository holds only the newest release.
  - The native app's own files (`settings.json`, `native-state.json`,
    `session.json`) stay, and the Tauri app ignores them.

## CI and repository

- CI installs the native setup over the real Tauri installers of 0.8.9 and
  0.8.10 on Windows and checks what the first start takes over (#433,
  #459). On Arch it upgrades from the 0.8.9 package.
- The first session check keeps a server the page already loaded (#435).
- Dependabot updates `main` weekly, and `AGENTS.md` asks to merge nothing
  else into `main` while a release is on its way.

## Open

- The real update path, from an installed Tauri app through the signed
  `latest.json` to the native app, runs for the first time with this
  release. CI starts the setup with the updater's arguments over 0.8.9 and
  0.8.10 only; updates from 0.7.0 to 0.8.8 are untested.
- The native app's own updater (0.9.0 to a later version) has not run end
  to end; CI covers its parts and unit tests.
- Whether SmartScreen stops a setup the app downloaded itself has not been
  tried; it carries no Mark of the Web.
- On Arch, the upgrade from 0.8.10's `legacy-settings.json` is covered by
  unit tests only; CI upgrades from 0.8.9.
- Tray, notifications, push-to-talk through the portal, real audio
  devices, cameras and the screen picker have not run in CI on a real
  desktop session.
- Installed 0.8.x Tauri apps on a 0.9.0 server show "Die Desktop-App ist
  veraltet … Hardware-Codecs wie AV1 und H.264"; the codec reason no longer
  fits, the update itself is right.
- On Linux, one finished `paplay` process stays after a call sound until the
  next sound or the app's end (#431).
